title: HiCI: Hierarchical Construction–Integration for Long-Context Attention
claim: A hierarchical module builds local segment summaries, integrates them into a global context, then broadcasts both to condition segment-level attention.
layout: Left Transformer block zoomed into right 3-stage stacked panels, top-to-bottom, dashed zoom lines
description: The figure has two parts. On the left is a narrow vertical Transformer block with Embedding, Norm, HiCI Attention, Norm, Feed Forward and residual plus-circles. Fire and snowflake icons mark trainable and frozen parts. Dashed lines zoom from the HiCI Attention box into a large rounded dashed panel on the right. The panel holds three stacked, color-coded stages. At the top, the input sequence is split into segments X1 to Xn. Stage 1, in blue, is Local Construction: shared slots and a bottleneck cross-attention produce local representations L1 to Ln. Stage 2, in cream, is Global Integration: multi-statistical aggregation (μ, μ+, μ−, σ, μ̂) feeds a compression bottleneck, cross-attention and a gate to produce G. Stage 3, in green, is Broadcast and Segment Attention: G and Li are prepended to each segment Xi, which goes into multi-head attention with LoRA. A grid shows the attention mask. Curved arrows connect the stages.
caption: Overview of HiCI. Left: HiCI integrated into a Transformer block; trainable components are highlighted. Right: HiCI constructs hierarchical context through three stages. (1) Local Construction: the input sequence is partitioned into $N$ segments, and cross-attention with $M$ learnable query slots extracts a local representation $L_i$ from each segment. (2) Global Integration: local representations $\{L_i\}_{i=1}^N$ are aggregated into a shared global context $G$ via multi-view statistical pooling and attention-based weighting. (3) Top-down Broadcast: $G$ and $L_i$ are prepended to each segment's key--value sequence, conditioning attention on hierarchical context while preserving parallelism across segments. At inference, HiCI is optionally applied during prefill, while autoregressive decoding uses standard attention.
abstract: Long-context language modeling is commonly framed as a scalability challenge of token-level attention, yet local-to-global information structuring remains largely implicit in existing approaches. Drawing on cognitive theories of discourse comprehension, we propose HiCI (Hierarchical Construction--Integration), a hierarchical attention module that constructs segment-level representations, integrates them into a shared global context, and broadcasts both to condition segment-level attention. We validate HiCI through parameter-efficient adaptation of LLaMA-2 with only <5.5% additional parameters, extending context from 4K to 100K tokens (7B) and 64K tokens (13B). Across language modeling, retrieval, and instruction-following benchmarks, HiCI yields consistent improvements over strong baselines, including matching proprietary models on topic retrieval and surpassing GPT-3.5-Turbo-16K on code comprehension. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of explicit hierarchical structuring as an inductive bias for long-context modeling.
